markdown_report:
The strongest early-stage proposal remains **terminal candidate competition**: retain corrected BERT4Rec and test terminal-branch cross-entropy over one positive and 32 uniformly sampled negatives. Treat this as a training intervention until matched controls distinguish objective, candidate-count and exclusion effects.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Terminal-prefix supervision matches appended-mask inference without revealing the target. Preserve this alignment. (2) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile margins and wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These training-position measurements motivate discrimination experiments, not validation claims. (3) Users identify broad resemblance displacing specific matches and historical interests displacing present priorities. Context-conditioned competition addresses both as hypotheses; histories cannot establish current intent, compatibility or ownership.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec supplies the retained masked-item backbone [1]. (2) Sampling studies report dataset-dependent tradeoffs, while PSL and UFNRec identify false-negative risks [2–4]. Start with uniform candidates rather than aggressive mining. (3) Loss reductions and negative counts can explain apparent architectural gains [5]. Sampled evaluation can also reverse full-catalog comparisons [6].

**Framework.** Objective competition addresses candidate separation; temporal attention addresses persistence; text fusion addresses attribute specificity. Their gaps are false negatives, unavailable target timestamps and semantic shortcuts, respectively. Evaluate objective changes through matched candidates and reductions before combining directions.

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal candidate competition | 3/6/6/8/4 | Originality: precise adaptation, established objective. Potential: informative controlled experiment, uncertain transfer. User: targets broad-match and stale-interest hypotheses, indirect mechanism. Model: trains separation, margins are scale-sensitive. Difficulty: unchanged serving, careful sampling and reduction integration. |
| Bucketed temporal attention | 5/7/7/5/7 | Originality: flexible BERT4Rec adaptation, established temporal relations. Potential: learn persistence, uncertain gains. User: models recency, cannot infer purpose. Model: may improve confusing cases, no measured temporal deficit. Difficulty: compact bias parameters, substantial timestamp/export integration. |
| Jointly learned title encoder | 4/7/7/5/8 | Originality: constrained joint fusion, established principle. Potential: finer attributes, sparse supervision. User: specific descriptors, resemblance shortcuts. Model: richer item features, no diagnosed semantic deficit. Difficulty: small encoder, extensive preprocessing/export work. |

**Selected experiment.** At 0% progress, retain the feasible objective intervention. Preserve terminal/interior sampling, branch coefficients and interior loss. Use 32 unique uniform negatives, excluding reserved tokens, target and training-history positives. Full-history exclusions use future-within-training information, without held-out labels; preserve the baseline policy for attributable comparisons [4].

First compare objectives at identical K, draws, temperature, scorer and reductions; otherwise label the result a bundled intervention. K=1 CE/BPR equivalence provides an algebraic check. Subsequently vary K alone if budget permits. Keep temperature at the canonical baseline value and retain norm behavior. Record branch gradients, clipping, embedding norms and runtime; unchanged coefficients do not ensure unchanged gradient balance.

Track fixed-panel ranks/hits alongside margins. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10; qualify gains as sampled-protocol results. Preserve seeds, routing, limits, diagnostic interfaces and one checkpoint/category. Record all attempts and checkpoint opportunities; paired user bootstrap, when outcomes are available, excludes training variability and selection bias [6–8]. Verify checkpoint/predictor parity. References appear below.

idea.description: Terminal candidate competition within one corrected BERT4Rec per category: test uniform 32-negative sampled cross-entropy for terminal-prefix targets while preserving the interior masked-item objective, bidirectional backbone, existing branch coefficients and appended-mask inference. Establish whether the host already uses this objective before proposing it as a change. Interpret an unmatched comparison as a bundled training intervention rather than evidence for cross-entropy alone.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly addresses two user-facing failures: broad associations outranking specific matches, and historical interests outranking recent priorities. At a leakage-free terminal prefix, multi-candidate competition requires the observed next target to outrank alternatives using the available recent context. This provides a testable training hypothesis, but neither cross-entropy nor uniform sampling explicitly distinguishes broad from specific items or stale from durable interests. The model-facing target is weak positive–negative separation, particularly Industrial_and_Scientific's margin p10=-0.2872 and Electronics' p10=-0.1374, with measured wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. Embedding similarity near 0.5 provides no evidence supporting an anti-collapse intervention. Temporal attention remains a reasonable subsequent direction if objective controls fail; text fusion requires more integration and carries the simulator's existing resemblance-shortcut risk.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate the supplied helpers into the corrected host baseline; they are not a standalone replacement train.py because baseline source, constructor, sampler settings and artifact interfaces were not supplied. Do not invent those interfaces or claim an executable end-to-end reproduction. Before execution, record the actual baseline terminal loss, K, exclusions, target reduction, temperature, scoring head, normalization, branch weights, optimizer, scheduler, clipping, sampling distribution, validation cadence and checkpoint tie-breaking. If the baseline already implements this intervention, select a genuine single-factor candidate-count comparison rather than repeating it under a new name.

Use K=32 unique uniformly sampled real-item negatives per terminal example, without replacement from the eligible catalog. The proposed policy excludes PAD, MASK, target ID and all observed training positives for that user. Construct exclusions solely from the training split. Full-training-history exclusion includes interactions later than the sampled endpoint: it is a legitimate offline convention but is not strictly chronological simulation. Prefix-only exclusion has different collision risks. Neither policy universally dominates, and unobserved candidates can still be relevant. For objective attribution, retain the baseline exclusion policy in every compared arm; if adopting full-history exclusions changes it, disclose the bundled change or test it separately. Always exclude the current positive explicitly.

Use a sorted eligible array and numpy.random.Generator.choice with replace=False and no probability weights. Cache arrays only when memory permits; otherwise rejection sampling from uniform real IDs is an exact alternative, rejecting excluded and already accepted IDs. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, use all eligible items and PAD-fill remaining slots; mask PAD logits from the denominator. Fail explicitly when no eligible negative exists. Report eligible counts, realized K and shortage frequency. This is a finite candidate objective, with no claim of unbiased full-softmax estimation and no sampling correction.

Retain stable item/user ordering and mappings. Use a dedicated seed-42 candidate RNG, separate from endpoint sampling, interior masks, model initialization, dropout and diagnostic RNG. For objective controls, use identically seeded candidate streams and identical sampled endpoints so draws match; do not load another trial's checkpoint or sampling artifacts. Assign reproducible category/worker streams using fixed category indices and SeedSequence, avoiding Python hash values and worker-scheduling-dependent shared RNG consumption. Pin or record library versions and deterministic settings. The helper assumes contiguous real IDs 1..itemnum; use the actual supplied mapping if this convention differs.

Keep terminal prefix construction leakage-free: choose the baseline endpoint, remove its target occurrence and every later interaction, truncate preceding history to maxlen-1, append the reserved MASK, and left-pad. Earlier repeated target occurrences remain legitimate history, even though the target ID is excluded from negatives. Do not provide target metadata or unavailable target timestamps. Preserve baseline interior masks, guaranteed supervised-target policy, interior loss, branch allocation and reductions. Average terminal cross-entropy across examples; if this differs from baseline reduction, identify it as an additional intervention. Preserve the optimizer, learning-rate schedule, regularization, validation cadence and checkpoint policy. Do not add protected-context dropout, hard mining, text features, temporal biases or a curriculum in this first comparison.

For clean objective attribution, compare cross-entropy and the baseline objective at the same K, negative draws, exclusion policy, temperature, scorer, normalization, terminal/interior coefficients and explicit target weights. Multi-negative cross-entropy redistributes pressure toward higher-scoring candidates; it is not merely K independent pairwise comparisons. With K=1, CE equals mean single-pair BPR at identical logits and temperature, providing an algebraic implementation check. Summed versus mean pairwise losses and BCE positive/negative weighting must be specified rather than silently changed. If the baseline K differs, a direct baseline-versus-CE32 result combines objective and candidate-count changes. Label it accordingly; prioritize a matched-K control before claiming an objective mechanism. Only subsequently vary K alone, reduction alone or temperature alone if the shared budget supports complete four-category trials. Each arm is a separate trial containing one independently trained model per category; never fuse arms.

Keep the canonical baseline temperature and embedding-normalization behavior, recording their values. Do not silently add cosine normalization, learned temperature or score rescaling. Positive inference-time temperature scaling alone preserves ranking. Raw margins can increase through norm growth without any ranking improvement. Preserve branch coefficients initially, but measure terminal/interior gradient norms, total clipping frequency, embedding norms and score dispersion: unchanged coefficients or matched scalar losses do not guarantee equivalent optimization. Adam and clipping prevent a simple learning-rate compensation from isolating objective effects. Probe gradient norms only on a small prespecified panel to limit diagnostic compute; use evaluation mode and torch.autograd.grad without optimizer updates, restore mode, and report that these gradients exclude training dropout.

The loss helper calls the actual model's log2feats and item_emb interfaces. Its default dot-product scorer is valid only if identical to the corrected baseline's scorer. If the baseline uses a transformation or bias, pass its canonical differentiable predict_score adapter, which must produce B x (K+1) logits. Verify the training scorer retains gradients; an inference-only decorated predict_score is unsuitable. No independent popularity, transition or text scorer is introduced.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl and every supplied route; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS=200 as the supplied environment default despite retaining BERT4Rec. Keep the same prespecified horizon, checkpoint opportunities and resource caps across completed controls. Train on one GPU and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. This trial trains exactly one independent model per category and exports one selected checkpoint per route. Do not inspect other trials, reuse trained checkpoints, average checkpoints, or combine independently fitted scores. All execution, diagnostics and failed attempts count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Record updates, supervised targets, realized candidate counts, runtime and incomplete runs; historical inspiration scores do not establish this intervention's improvement.

Keep the canonical predictor writer unchanged only if architecture and serving scorer are unchanged. Save architecture configuration, item mapping, PAD/MASK IDs, maxlen, positional convention and selected state_dict, then strictly reload. Verify exact checkpoint state identity and finite matching evaluation scores across the actual trained module, factory reload, ModelView and generated working/predict.py. Cover short, full-length, overlength/truncated, mixed-length and singleton inputs with identical candidates, padding and mask placement; use atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 alongside deterministic ranking checks. Serving retains intact observed histories and appended-mask inference; use the greatest nonpadding index, never nonpadding_count-1. Preserve correct attention padding masks and deterministic evaluation dropout behavior. A training-only loss requires no new serving computation.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and the actual trained view.model. Preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Set dataset identity correctly. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Measure margins only at valid supervised MASK positions. Report terminal and interior subsets separately only when provenance is available; do not infer provenance from tensor shape. Use frozen diagnostic examples and negatives independent of training RNG and common across comparisons. Document whether each diagnostic reports one-negative pairwise ordering or multi-candidate rank. Keep existing measurements comparable rather than replacing their negative sampling silently.

Add descriptive positive ranks, diagnostic candidate-set hits@10 and the fraction with at least ten negatives scoring above the positive, using a fixed panel and a declared tie rule matching the host when known. These diagnostics are distinct from host validation and full-catalog recommendations. Raw margins are scale-dependent, and pairwise success can miss the top-10 boundary. Optional normalized margins are supplemental, not replacements for original definitions. No ratings, reviews, product categories, prices, stores or simulator traits are available; category breakdowns must be marked unavailable rather than inferred from empty lists. Preserve unavailable flags for probes whose gates fail. User immediate-choice, explicit mismatch and unidentified-item feedback remain separate qualitative outcomes; unidentified skips are not negative preference labels.

Select exclusively through the pinned macro validation HR@10: 200 users per category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Do not alter the evaluator, splits, candidate generation or held-out access. Improvements apply to this sampled protocol and cannot establish full-catalog HR@10 superiority. Twenty real training users, five per category, still receive the required full-catalog unseen-item recommendations as a separate qualitative diagnostic. Uniform candidate training may favor popularity or easy alternatives; inspect training-frequency and history-length strata descriptively without fitting an auxiliary score or changing selection.

Prespecify a small number of comparisons and record every evaluated hypothesis and checkpoint opportunity. If existing host outputs expose paired per-user hit indicators, use 500 CPU bootstrap replicates with seed 42: resample users with replacement independently within each category, preserve both models' outcomes together, and average the four category differences equally. Report a percentile 95% interval, conditional on fixed fitted checkpoints and evaluation candidates. It excludes training-seed and candidate-sampling variation and does not correct repeated-validation selection bias. One hit changes category HR@10 by 0.005 and macro HR@10 by 0.00125. If paired outcomes are unavailable, report that limitation without reconstructing or inventing them. Do not add seed search, validation-driven temperature sweeps or hidden-test access.

User Diagnosis Alignment: 6/10. Positive: explicitly tests broad-match competition and insufficient emphasis on recent observed context. Negative: neither the uniform sampler nor CE directly identifies specificity, stale interests, compatibility, duplication or present purpose. Model Diagnosis Alignment: 8/10. Positive: directly trains relative candidate separation in the two categories with weak measured margin tails. Negative: training margins depend on score scale and sampling, and improvements need not transfer to host HR@10. Originality remains 3/10; future potential is revised from 7 to 6 because mechanisms and generalization are uncertain; code difficulty rises from 3 to 4 because controlled sampling, reductions and diagnostic/export compatibility require more work than changing a loss function.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def candidate_rng(category_index, worker_index=0):
    # Fixed category ordering; independent of training/sampler/dropout RNG.
    seed = np.random.SeedSequence([42, 32001, category_index, worker_index])
    return np.random.default_rng(seed)


def sample_uniform_negatives(targets, exclusion_sets, itemnum, rng, K=32):
    """CPU sampling, real IDs 1..itemnum. Exclusions use training only.

    exclusion_sets must follow the prespecified policy shared by controls.
    Full-history exclusion is offline training, not chronological simulation.
    This simple reference version materializes each eligible array; cache
    only when affordable or use exact uniform rejection sampling.
    """
    if K < 1 or itemnum < 2:
        raise ValueError('Invalid catalog or candidate count')
    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=np.int64)
    if targets.ndim != 1 or len(exclusion_sets) != len(targets):
        raise ValueError('Invalid sampling inputs')
    result = np.zeros((len(targets), K), dtype=np.int64)
    realized = np.zeros(len(targets), dtype=np.int64)
    catalog = np.arange(1, itemnum + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    for row, (target, excluded) in enumerate(zip(targets, exclusion_sets)):
        if not 1 <= int(target) <= itemnum:
            raise ValueError('Target must be a real item')
        blocked = {int(x) for x in excluded if 1 <= int(x) <= itemnum}
        blocked.add(int(target))
        # Sorting makes construction stable regardless of set iteration order.
        blocked_ids = np.asarray(sorted(blocked), dtype=np.int64)
        eligible = catalog[~np.isin(catalog, blocked_ids)]
        k = min(K, len(eligible))
        if k == 0:
            raise ValueError('No eligible negative; report sampler failure')
        result[row, :k] = rng.choice(eligible, size=k, replace=False)
        realized[row] = k
    return result, realized


def final_nonpadding_index(sequence):
    """LEFT padding and internal PAD holes; PAD=0."""
    if sequence.ndim != 2 or sequence.shape[1] == 0:
        raise ValueError('Expected a nonempty B x L sequence')
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1
    ).amax(dim=1)
    if bool(last.lt(0).any()):
        raise ValueError('Empty terminal sequence')
    return last


def terminal_candidate_loss(model, sequence, target, negatives, mask_id,
                            score_fn=None, temperature=1.0):
    """One jointly trained BERT4Rec; no serving-time score fusion.

    sequence: B x L, leakage-free prefix ending in reserved MASK.
    target: B real item IDs.
    negatives: B x K unique eligible real IDs, PAD=0 for shortages only.
    Caller enforces the declared training-only exclusion policy.
    score_fn(features, items): canonical differentiable B x (K+1) logits.
    Default scorer requires the baseline's exact dot-product scoring rule.
    temperature must equal the recorded baseline value in matched controls;
    use 1.0 if the canonical scorer already includes baseline temperature.
    All tensors must be on the model device with integer token IDs.
    """
    if not np.isfinite(temperature) or temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Temperature must be finite and positive')
    if sequence.ndim != 2 or target.ndim != 1 or negatives.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError('Invalid tensor dimensions')
    if sequence.shape[0] != target.shape[0] or negatives.shape[0] != target.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Batch dimensions differ')
    if not bool(((sequence >= 0) & (sequence <= mask_id)).all()):
        raise ValueError('Invalid sequence IDs')
    if not bool(((target > 0) & (target < mask_id)).all()):
        raise ValueError('Targets must be real items')
    if not bool(((negatives >= 0) & (negatives < mask_id)).all()):
        raise ValueError('Invalid negative IDs')
    valid_negative = negatives.ne(0)
    if not bool(valid_negative.any(dim=1).all()):
        raise ValueError('Each example needs an eligible negative')
    if bool((negatives.eq(target[:, None]) & valid_negative).any()):
        raise ValueError('Target included among negatives')
    ordered = negatives.sort(dim=1).values
    if bool((ordered[:, 1:].eq(ordered[:, :-1]) & ordered[:, 1:].ne(0)).any()):
        raise ValueError('Duplicate negative IDs')

    last = final_nonpadding_index(sequence)
    rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)
    if not bool(sequence[rows, last].eq(mask_id).all()):
        raise ValueError('Terminal readout must be reserved MASK')
    if not bool(sequence.eq(mask_id).sum(dim=1).eq(1).all()):
        raise ValueError('Expected exactly one terminal MASK')
    if not bool(((sequence > 0) & (sequence < mask_id)).any(dim=1).all()):
        raise ValueError('Terminal examples require visible history')

    features = model.log2feats(sequence)[rows, last]
    candidates = torch.cat((target[:, None], negatives), dim=1)
    if score_fn is None:
        logits = torch.einsum('bd,bkd->bk', features,
                              model.item_emb(candidates))
    else:
        logits = score_fn(features, candidates)
    if logits.shape != candidates.shape:
        raise ValueError('Canonical scorer returned incompatible shape')
    invalid = torch.cat((torch.zeros_like(target[:, None], dtype=torch.bool),
                         ~valid_negative), dim=1)
    logits = logits.float() / temperature
    if not bool(torch.isfinite(logits[~invalid]).all()):
        raise ValueError('Nonfinite valid candidate logits')
    logits = logits.masked_fill(invalid, float('-inf'))
    labels = torch.zeros(target.shape[0], dtype=torch.long,
                         device=target.device)
    return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels, reduction='mean')


def check_one_negative_ce_bpr():
    # Algebraic check only; no training, datasets or benchmark claims.
    positive = torch.tensor([-2.0, 0.0, 3.0], dtype=torch.float64)
    negative = torch.tensor([1.0, -1.0, 0.5], dtype=torch.float64)
    temperature = 1.0
    scores = torch.stack((positive, negative), dim=1) / temperature
    ce = F.cross_entropy(scores, torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.long),
                         reduction='none')
    bpr = F.softplus((negative - positive) / temperature)
    torch.testing.assert_close(ce, bpr, atol=1e-12, rtol=1e-12)


# Integration specification; retain supplied baseline infrastructure:

# Audit actual baseline loss, K, exclusions, reductions, scorer and temperature.
# Prespecify ONE arm per trial; never fuse independently fitted arms.

#   initialize ONE corrected BERT4Rec with training seed 42

#   for each configured epoch (<=200; environment default 200):

#           terminal, interior = supplied_corrected_sampler()
#           # Endpoint target and all later events are absent from input.
#           # Input = left_pad(prefix[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK]).
#           negatives_np, realized_K = sample_uniform_negatives(
#               terminal.target.cpu().numpy(), declared_training_exclusions,
#               itemnum, rng, K=32)
#           negatives = torch.as_tensor(negatives_np, dtype=torch.long,
#                                       device=model_device)
#           Lt = terminal_candidate_loss(
#               model, terminal.sequence, terminal.target, negatives, MASK,
#               canonical_differentiable_score_fn, baseline_temperature)
#           Li = unchanged_baseline_interior_loss(model, interior)
#           loss = unchanged_alpha * Lt + (1-unchanged_alpha) * Li
#           unchanged_optimizer_update(loss)
#           record_updates_targets_realized_K_clipping_and_runtime()
#       apply_unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()
#   save_one_selected_checkpoint_with_complete_configuration(category)
#   verify_exact_reload_and_ModelView_exported_predictor_parity()
#   preserve_and_run_required_diagnosis_with_definitions_and_availability()
# Export exactly one selected checkpoint per category via canonical writer.
# Preserve all four routes and required twenty-user full-catalog diagnostics.
# Host independently evaluates fixed macro validation HR@10.
# Matched objective controls use identical K/draws/exclusions/temperature,
# reductions, scorer, weights, updates and checkpoint opportunities.
# If K or exclusions differ from baseline, report a bundled intervention.
# No checkpoint reuse, independent score fusion, or held-out-label exclusions.

originality.positive: A narrowly specified terminal-only intervention and matched candidate controls distinguish the experiment from the earlier dropout and curriculum directions.
originality.negative: Multi-negative cross-entropy, terminal masked prediction and uniform sampling are established; neither the combination nor its user-facing mechanism establishes a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could clarify candidate competition versus candidate-count effects and motivate false-negative-robust objectives within the same BERT4Rec network.
future_potential.negative: Uniform candidates may remain easy, gains may reflect exclusion or popularity effects, and sampled-validation improvements may not transfer to full-catalog choices or specific current needs.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention adds no serving parameters or inference computation and can reuse the corrected backbone and predictor writer.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient exact sampling, reproducible streams, loss-reduction controls, differentiable canonical scoring, diagnostic provenance and checkpoint/export parity require careful integration; no executable baseline source was supplied.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer [1]
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Provides the retained backbone and masked-target formulation.
limitations: Does not establish that terminal-only 32-negative cross-entropy improves the pinned benchmark.
Terminal supervision already has precedent, limiting novelty claims.

related_work.title: Sequential-recommendation negative-sampling comparison supplied in the search results [2]
contributions: The supplied summary reports dataset-dependent tradeoffs among random, popularity, in-batch and adaptive sampling.
limitations: Supports controlled sampling comparisons rather than a universal advantage for harder or uniform negatives.
Does not establish gains under this task's fixed splits and candidates.

related_work.title: Pairwise Softmax Loss [3]
contributions: The supplied summary identifies false-negative sensitivity and proposes alternative pairwise activations.
limitations: The selected experiment implements ordinary sampled cross-entropy rather than PSL.
Its false-negative robustness cannot be transferred to the proposed loss.

related_work.title: UFNRec: False-negative handling in sequential recommendation [4]
contributions: Documents the false-negative problem in sequential recommendation.
Motivates explicit exclusion policies and caution about treating unobserved items as verified negatives.
limitations: Does not establish a universal winner between prefix-only and full-training-history exclusion.
Excluding known positives does not eliminate unknown relevant candidates.

related_work.title: SASRec/BERT4Rec reproduction experiments supplied in the reflection results [5]
contributions: Supports auditing loss formulation and negative count when comparing sequential recommenders.
Motivates separating objective, reduction and candidate-count changes.
limitations: Does not establish the best objective or candidate count for this pinned task.
Serves as methodological evidence; the comparison model family remains BERT4Rec.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation [6]
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons relative to full-catalog metrics.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host's pinned evaluation protocol.
A sampled validation gain must remain qualified to its evaluation setting.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation [7]
contributions: Explains paired resampling, supporting preservation of corresponding model outcomes during user bootstrap.
limitations: The proposed macro-average bootstrap additionally requires independent resampling within each category.
Conditional intervals exclude training and candidate variability and do not correct adaptive selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation [8]
contributions: Establishes how model selection can overfit an evaluation criterion and bias reported performance.
limitations: Does not quantify the selection bias of this particular search.
Recording attempts and reporting bootstrap intervals cannot remove that bias.

related_work.title: Original SASRec training sampler
contributions: Provides a documented precedent for excluding all items in a user's training history from negatives.
limitations: Includes future-within-training information when sampling an earlier endpoint.
Is a sampling precedent only and does not authorize replacing the BERT4Rec backbone.

related_work.title: Global-chronology evaluation analysis supplied in the reflection results
contributions: Warns that ignoring global chronology can distort evaluation.
limitations: Does not authorize altering the supplied splits or establish a universal exclusion policy.

related_work.title: NumPy Generator.choice documentation
contributions: Documents uniform sampling without replacement when replace=False and probability weights are omitted.
limitations: Uniformity depends on constructing the correct eligible population.
Materializing per-user eligible arrays can be expensive.

related_work.title: NumPy parallel random-number generation documentation
contributions: Describes SeedSequence-based reproducible stream construction.
limitations: Reproducibility still requires stable mappings, stream assignment, execution policy and recorded library versions.

related_work.title: CE/BPR theoretical analysis supplied in the reflection results
contributions: Supports the equivalence of one-negative cross-entropy and BPR at matched scores and temperature.
limitations: The equivalence does not extend to multi-negative cross-entropy versus an independent pairwise mean.
Does not predict which objective improves the pinned validation metric.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax study supplied in the reflection results
contributions: Motivates treating temperature, normalization and embedding norms as interacting experimental factors.
limitations: Temperature effects cannot be reduced to a universally increasing gradient magnitude.
Does not establish a suitable temperature for this task.

related_work.title: Subset-only softmax-estimation limitation supplied in the search results
contributions: The supplied summary identifies a general bias limitation for subset-only softmax estimators.
limitations: Does not imply that every finite-candidate training objective is ineffective.
The selected experiment claims neither unbiased full-softmax estimation nor a correction overcoming this limitation.

related_work.title: TiSASRec
contributions: Introduces temporal relations alongside positional information, motivating the alternative bucketed-time attention direction.
limitations: Adapting temporal relations to BERT4Rec requires inference-matched unknown-time handling for masked targets.
Does not establish benefits for the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: DenseRec (2025)
contributions: Studies alignment between pretrained content embeddings and collaborative item representations.
Warns that semantic similarity can obscure differences in item appeal.
limitations: Its pretrained content setup is unavailable under this task's constraints.
Does not establish the proposed randomly initialized title encoder within BERT4Rec.
